root.claim: A single deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.

motivation.text: Scanning the whole array at each of the Theta(log n) transform levels already costs n log n, so a saving is needed in both data movement and arithmetic, and these are what the two tape procedures supply.

root.salient: The saving is a genuine power of the logarithm, yet $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small: it comes from the strict inequality $s<Wm$ for fixed finite networks, which survives as exponents $\tau,\lambda'<1$ in two tape procedures, and every other cost has power of $p$ at most $1-2\kappa$.
